title: The Side Experiment That Outgrew Nupedia in January 2001
conflicts: Founding credit: Sanger (2005 memoir) claims the wiki idea, the name and early organising while crediting Wales with the encyclopedia idea and funding; Wales (AP 2007; wikipedia-l 2005; Lex Fridman 2023) says Jeremy Rosenfeld showed him wikis first, called Sanger a subordinate and the co-founder claim 'absurd', yet says Sanger is under-credited. Both given, attributed, not adjudicated. Wales's 'almost two years' of Nupedia conflicts with its early-2000 start; paraphrased. Nupedia article count (about 25 vs 'just over 20') attributed to Sanger.
notes: Funding changed from slate's 'nonprofit' to 'bootstrapped': in 2001 Bomis, Wales's private company, paid for both projects; the Wikimedia Foundation came later. The episode is the side-launch of the wiki, not an outright abandonment of Nupedia, which continued alongside. Primary sources include Sanger's archived 10 January 2001 Nupedia-l posts (Internet Archive), read in full via plain curl because WebFetch cannot reach web.archive.org.
